stages.name: Independent
stages.desc: City-states, kingdoms and peoples outside the great powers

stages.name: Mitannian
stages.desc: Lands ruled directly by the Hurrian kingdom of Mitanni

stages.name: Mitannian vassal
stages.desc: Syrian kings bound by oath to Mitanni: Aleppo, Alalakh, Ugarit

stages.name: Egypt
stages.desc: The New Kingdom of the pharaohs

stages.name: Egyptian-controlled
stages.desc: Canaanite cities that swore loyalty to Egypt after Thutmose III

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Alashiya: copper-mining towns such as Enkomi trade with the Syrian coast

states.name: Israel
timeline: Canaanite city-states such as Megiddo and Hazor
Thutmose I's army marches north through Canaan to the Euphrates
After the battle of Megiddo, the princes of Canaan swear loyalty to Thutmose III

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Canaanite towns; Ahmose's army besieges the last Hyksos stronghold at Sharuhen
Gaza becomes Egypt's main base in Canaan

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Canaanite port cities, Byblos, Sidon and Tyre, and the hill town of Ammiya
Idrimi lives in exile at Ammiya among refugees and Habiru warriors
Thutmose III's campaigns on the coast bring the Lebanese ports under Egypt

states.name: Syria
timeline: The kingdom of Aleppo, Ugarit and the city-states of Syria, two generations after a Hittite army sacked Aleppo
A disaster at Aleppo drives Idrimi's family into exile at Emar
The Hurrian kings of Mitanni become overlords of Aleppo, Mukish, Ugarit and the north Syrian kingdoms; their capital, Washukanni, lies on the upper Khabur
Idrimi swears an oath to Barattarna of Mitanni and rules Alalakh as his vassal
Idrimi's son Niqmepa rules Alalakh under Saushtatar of Mitanni

states.name: Turkey
timeline: The Hittite kingdom rules central Anatolia from Hattusa, weakened by murders at court; Alalakh, in today's Hatay, belongs to the Syrian world
Telipinu's edict tries to end the royal killings and fixes the order of succession
Idrimi of Alalakh raids the Hittite borderlands and burns seven towns
Kizzuwatna in Cilicia makes a treaty with Idrimi and leans towards Mitanni

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Kassite kings rule Babylon; Ashur is a small independent city-state on the Tigris
Mitanni's realm reaches east across the Jazira to Nineveh and Arrapha; Babylonia in the south stays Kassite
Saushtatar of Mitanni sacks Ashur and carries off its doors of silver and gold

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Small towns and pastoral peoples east of the Jordan
Pella and a few other towns appear in Thutmose III's lists, but Egypt does not rule the highlands

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Ahmose's New Kingdom reunites Egypt after expelling the Hyksos
Hatshepsut rules for the boy king Thutmose III, then as pharaoh herself
Thutmose III, now sole ruler, leads his army into Canaan

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Northern Cyprus, part of the copper-rich land of Alashiya

events.title: Aleppo rebuilt
events.text: Kings of Aleppo rule northern Syria again, two generations after the Hittite king Mursili sacked the city.

events.title: Siege of Sharuhen
events.text: Pharaoh Ahmose besieges the last Hyksos stronghold in southern Canaan for three years.

events.title: Kassite Babylon
events.text: A Kassite dynasty rules Babylon, which the Hittites had raided in 1595 BC.

events.title: Telipinu's edict
events.text: The Hittite king Telipinu lays down rules of succession after decades of royal murders.

events.title: Amenhotep I
events.text: Amenhotep I succeeds Ahmose at Thebes and consolidates the New Kingdom.

events.title: Kizzuwatna treaty
events.text: Telipinu makes a treaty as equals with Isputahsu, king of Kizzuwatna in Cilicia.

events.title: Mitanni rises
events.text: Hurrian princes with Indo-Aryan names build the kingdom of Mitanni around Washukanni.

events.title: Disaster at Aleppo
events.text: An 'evil deed' in Aleppo, never explained, forces the family of Ilim-ilimma to flee.

events.title: Refuge at Emar
events.text: The family shelters with Idrimi's mother's kin at Emar on the Euphrates.

events.title: Thutmose I
events.text: Thutmose I becomes pharaoh and turns Egypt's armies towards Asia.

events.title: Across the desert
events.text: Idrimi takes his horse, chariot and groom and crosses the desert, spending a night among Sutean nomads.

events.title: Arrival at Ammiya
events.text: At Ammiya in Canaan, refugees from Aleppo, Mukish and Niya recognise him as their lord's son.

events.title: Among the Habiru
events.text: Idrimi lives seven years among the Habiru, uprooted warriors and outlaws of the hills.

events.title: Thutmose at the Euphrates
events.text: Thutmose I marches through Syria and sets up a victory stela on the Euphrates.

events.title: Mitanni moves west
events.text: Mitanni's kings become overlords of the north Syrian kingdoms from the Euphrates to the sea.

events.title: Omens of birds
events.text: Idrimi releases birds and reads the entrails of lambs; in the seventh year, he writes, the storm god turned to him.

events.title: Boats and an army
events.text: Idrimi builds ships and puts soldiers aboard for the voyage north.

events.title: Landing at Mount Casius
events.text: He lands below Mount Casius, the storm god's mountain, and the land of Mukish rallies to him.

events.title: Alalakh welcomes him
events.text: Niya, Ama'u, Mukish and Alalakh accept Idrimi 'as one man'.

events.title: Barattarna's hostility
events.text: For seven years, Barattarna, king of Mitanni, treats Idrimi as an enemy.

events.title: Thutmose II
events.text: Thutmose II succeeds his father; Egypt's push into Asia pauses.

events.title: Oath with Barattarna
events.text: Idrimi recalls his ancestors' oaths to the Hurrian kings; Barattarna accepts him as vassal.

events.title: King of Alalakh
events.text: Idrimi takes the throne of Alalakh, capital of Mukish on the Orontes plain.

events.title: Raid on Hatti
events.text: Idrimi's army raids the Hittite borderlands and sacks seven towns, among them Zaruna.

events.title: A new palace
events.text: With the plunder of the raid, Idrimi builds a palace at Alalakh.

events.title: Settling the uprooted
events.text: Idrimi gives homes to the wandering people of his land and settles them.

events.title: Treaty with Pilliya
events.text: Idrimi and Pilliya of Kizzuwatna agree to return each other's fugitives; the tablet survives.

events.title: Hatshepsut regent
events.text: The boy Thutmose III becomes pharaoh; his aunt and stepmother Hatshepsut governs.

events.title: Hatshepsut crowned
events.text: Hatshepsut takes the full titles of pharaoh and builds her temple at Deir el-Bahari.

events.title: Ugarit's harbour
events.text: Ugarit, Alalakh's southern neighbour, trades with Cyprus, Egypt and the Aegean under Mitanni's shadow.

events.title: Copper of Alashiya
events.text: Cyprus ships copper from towns such as Enkomi to the ports of Syria.

events.title: Thirty years
events.text: Idrimi's statue says he ruled thirty years and set down his deeds on his own image.

events.title: Niqmepa succeeds
events.text: Idrimi's son Niqmepa rules Alalakh; his archives survive in the Level IV palace.

events.title: Thutmose III alone
events.text: Hatshepsut dies and Thutmose III rules alone.

events.title: Battle of Megiddo
events.text: Thutmose III defeats a Canaanite coalition led by the king of Kadesh and besieges Megiddo for seven months.

events.title: Canaan submits
events.text: The princes of Canaan swear loyalty to Egypt; their sons are taken to Egypt as hostages.

events.title: Ashur sacked
events.text: Saushtatar of Mitanni sacks Ashur and carries its silver and gold doors to Washukanni.

events.title: Phoenician coast
events.text: Thutmose III campaigns against Ullaza and Ardata on the Lebanese coast.

events.title: Byblos and cedar
events.text: Byblos supplies Egypt's armies with cedar timber and ships.

events.title: Kadesh attacked
events.text: Thutmose III strikes at Kadesh on the Orontes, Mitanni's ally in the south.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's Turkey, Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, Jordan, Cyprus, Egypt and Iraq, by the power that dominated most of each modern country. Regions are today's boundaries; ancient borders were fluid, Mitanni's heartland lay in today's north-east Syria, and Alalakh itself sits in Turkey's Hatay. A simplification: dates are approximate and follow the middle chronology.
